answer_1.quote: In the past few years, Text-To-Speech (TTS) models have made a lot of progress in synthesizing human-like speech.
answer_1.outputs: speech samples with diverse prosody patterns

answer_2.quote: We conduct quantitative evaluations for our DPP-TTS, DPP-TTS w/o PDM, and VITS with high temperature. We have used the following metrics for evaluating our model and the baseline. σ_p: phoneme-level standard deviation of duration or pitch in a speech. This metric reflects the prosodic diversity inside each speech sample. Determinant: a determinant of the similarity matrix is used to evaluate the diversity among prosodic features of 10 generated samples.

answer_4.quote: Via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), we assign ten testers living in the United States to a pair of audio samples (i.e., DPP-TTS and a baseline), and ask them to listen to audio samples and choose among three options: A: sample A has more varied prosody than sample B, Same: sample A and B are equally varied in prosody, B: the opposite of first option.
answer_4.guideline: testers are asked to listen to audio samples and choose among three options: A: sample A has more varied prosody than sample B, Same: sample A and B are equally varied in prosody, B: the opposite of first option.
